text:
lee: noticed a cache hit-rate drop (~18%) after this morning's kernel bump. attaching quick profile snippets. :frowning:
lee: suspecting cache key divergence from tokenizer changes + system prompt tweaks
maria: did we land any normalization or system-prompt formatting PRs overnight?
ajay: what does the tokenization look like for a small repro? paste sample inputs + token ids if you have them
lee: here's a tiny example from canary vs prod:
```
prefix_raw: "Translate to French: What's the time?"
old_token_ids: [101, 202, 33]
new_token_ids: [101, 303, 33]
old_key: sha1(norm_old + tok_v0.13.2) -> 0x8b2f...
new_key: sha1(norm_new + tok_v0.13.3) -> 0x7c4d...
```
lee: same visible text but token ids diverged -> misses
devon: that points to a tokenizer package bump (BPE changes). which tokenizers version is in the new runtime image?
lee: runtime image tag: rdw-runtime:2026-03-18-kernelv2 (we pulled latest wheel, didn't pin tokenizers)
maria: quick follow: PR #4021 changed system-prompt rendering to strip trailing newlines, and CI also updated tokenizers to 0.13.3 in base image
ajay: combination of both explains subtle key changes (norm + token id mapping). need either canonical text-normalization stable across releases OR include tokenizer version in key namespace
devon: proposal: canonicalize on text-level before tokenization using stable rules (unicode NFKC, collapse whitespace, normalize quotes) + stable ordering for tool/function call fields. include explicit key-version and tokenizer-version in the cache key metadata
ops: warmup idea: backfill top prefixes under both key-versions for a short window to smooth rollouts
lee: also saw kernel batching heuristics changed effective batch size from 2->4 for short prefixes which increased contention on KV lookup path; profiling shows a small window where we hit an extra context switch and 90th pct latency regressed ~30ms
infra-bot: deploy canary v2026-03-18-kernelv2 reported: 12/50 canary requests missed cache vs 2/50 baseline (alerting threshold exceeded)
maria: short-term mitigation: pin tokenizers in runtime image to the previous release and roll canary back, long-term: implement canonicalizer + key-versioning
ajay: implementation notes: key composition we should use something like:
```
key = sha1(norm_text) + '::' + 'kver=v2' + '::' + 'tok=0.13.2' + '::' + join(sorted(tool_sig))
```
devon: and lookup flow: try current key -> if miss, try fallback variants (tok old, norm old) for first 24h, log fallback hits to metrics
ops: fallback adds an extra KV read on misses; cost vs missing inference is worth it for the migration window
lee: edge-case: system prompts are injected server-side; if prompt text changed (e.g., trailing newline trim) that will flip keys even with same tokenizer. we need deterministic injection ordering and a prompt-version tag in key metadata
maria: agree — add prompt_version to key suffix, bump when we change server-injected prompts
ajay: plan for rollout:
- pin tokenizers in runtime image and rollback immediate canary (maria)
- add text-normalizer library + unit tests (maria)
- implement key-version suffix + fallback lookup (devon)
- add telemetry for fallback hits and top-prefix diffs (ajay)
- run warmup backfill job for top 5k prefixes across key variants (ops)
lee: I'll open a tracking ticket INF-4512 and link PRs, also schedule a quick postmortem if hit-rate doesn't recover after mitigation
maria: opening pin + normalizer PRs now :keyboard_face:
ajay: I'll prototype fallback and metric collection, will push a canary flag behind FF
ops: I'll coordinate the warmup backfill once we have key-version keys available — estimate 2h run for 5k prefixes on staging KV cluster
devon: small snippet for normalization we can port in Rust/Go to runtime for performance:
```
fn normalize(s: &str) -> String {
  s.nfkc().trim().replace_regex("\\s+", " ").to_lowercase()
}
```
lee: final note: kernel selection and batching heuristics intersect with this — larger batch sizes amplify the miss penalty. when we change kernel defaults, run a quick cache-sensitivity test to see hit-rate delta
infra-bot: rollback triggered for rdw-runtime:2026-03-18-kernelv2 canary
ops: I'll queue the backfill after the key-version PR merges.
lee: thanks all, tracking owners above. please ack on INF-4512 when PRs are up :thumbsup:
